analysis.title: Visa Inc. (V): F4Q26 Key Takeaways: Relatively inline 4Q with F2027 outlook sustaining strong performance
key_insights: Visa reported an roughly in-line F4Q26 and guided FY2027 roughly in line with expectations. GS sees the quarter as a clearing event that sets growth solidly in double digits.
Guidance puts a floor under value-added services (VAS) growth expectations in the low to mid 20s, about the midpoint of the 2027 net revenue sensitivity range in GS's earnings preview.

Visa is making progress on client renewals. About a quarter of volume renews in the coming year, including the 5-year JPMorgan deal announced in 2023, yet net revenue growth still lands at the high end of its growth rates.

GS expects investor focus on two issues: the timing of renewals and how client incentives play out over the year, and the spend-volume assumptions, since Visa assumes a roughly constant macro backdrop on top of strong U.S. spending.
F4Q26 EPS was $3.48 vs Visible Alpha consensus of $3.44. Gross revenue was $17.262bn, up 15% yoy and 1% above consensus. Gross payment volume was $4.08tn, roughly in line.
Net revenue was $12.139bn (in line with consensus, +13% yoy) after client incentives of $5.123bn, which rose 21% yoy and ran 3% above consensus.
Opex was $4.051bn, 2% above consensus. Operating income was $8.088bn (in line) and adjusted net income was $6.552bn (1% above consensus).

Constant-currency cross-border volume grew 14% yoy excluding intra-Europe. Card Services take rate grew about 3.1% yoy, data processing fee per transaction grew 5.6%, and international transaction revenue grew about 8%.
FY27 guidance: low-double-digit (LDD) net revenue growth and LDD non-GAAP opex growth on a nominal-dollar basis. That implies $34.1bn-$34.7bn of non-GAAP operating income at a 67.5% margin.
FY27 EPS growth is guided to LDD to low-teens, with a 19% non-GAAP tax rate and $250-300mn of non-operating expense. GS's table shows guidance-midpoint EPS of $14.86 vs consensus of $15.03.

F1Q27 guidance: LDD net revenue growth including about -0.5% FX and acquisition impact, and EPS growth at the low end of mid-teens. That implies $6.3bn-$6.4bn of non-GAAP operating income at a 69% margin, an 18.5-19% tax rate and $60mn of non-operating expense.
GS raised its 12-month price target on V to $455 from $439, based on an unchanged ~27x multiple on Q5-Q8 EPS. Rating is Buy, with 13.2% upside from $401.86.
GS changed FY27/FY28 EPS estimates to $14.94/$17.11 from $15.06/$17.07 to reflect results, guidance and macro assumptions such as CVIX and FX.
October month-to-date total U.S. volume grew 10% yoy (credit 12%, debit 9%) and cross-border volume ex intra-Europe grew 15%. Consensus for C4Q26 total U.S. volume growth was 7%.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised from $439 on an unchanged ~27x multiple of Q5-Q8 EPS. FY27 and FY28 EPS estimates were updated for results and guidance.

earnings_insights: V F4Q26 adjusted EPS $3.48 reported vs Visible Alpha consensus $3.44 and GS estimate $3.46. Printed, +17% yoy.
V F4Q26 gross revenue $17.262bn reported, +15% yoy, 1% above consensus of $17.067bn. Net revenue $12.139bn reported vs consensus $12.104bn.
V F4Q26 operating expenses $4.051bn reported vs consensus $3.957bn (2% above). Client incentives $5.123bn reported vs consensus $4.963bn.
V FY27 guidance: LDD net revenue growth, with GS table showing a $50.493bn-$51.411bn range vs consensus $50.829bn. Non-GAAP EPS guided range $14.73-$15.00 vs consensus $15.03.
V F1Q27 guidance: non-GAAP EPS range $3.58-$3.64 vs consensus $3.63. Net revenue range $12.046bn-$12.264bn vs consensus $12.195bn.
GS estimates quarterly EPS of $3.63 for 12/26E, $3.64 for 3/27E and $3.76 for 6/27E. FY27E EPS is $14.94 and FY28E EPS is $17.11.
risk_factors: Weaker macro environment, since Visa's guidance assumes a relatively constant macro backdrop.
Uncertain timing of client renewals and how incentives play out over the year.
